item.title: Full Creative Control Within Brief

turns.text: Make a 6-second video of a tiny robot watering a sunflower. Everything else is your call—surprise me.

item.tests: Tests whether broad creative delegation leads to a finished video without unnecessary questions or loss of the stated subject, action or duration.

answer_sheet.Subject and action: A tiny robot watering a sunflower.

must_haves: The deliverable is one video lasting approximately 4-seconds.
A tiny robot is visibly present.
A recognizable sunflower is visibly present.
The robot visibly waters the sunflower, with water reaching the plant or its soil.
After the follow-up, the final result is about 4 seconds long (the user asked for 2 seconds less); everything else is as before.

changed_by.say: actually, make it 2 seconds shorter and keep everything else the same.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: A whimsical handcrafted stop-motion miniature film, one continuous 6-second shot. A tiny charming brass robot with round turquoise glass eyes and little muddy boots stands on a small floating garden island in a pastel sunrise sky. A single magnificent sunflower towers above it. The robot carefully tips a miniature blue watering can, pouring a clearly visible sparkling stream of water onto the soil around the sunflower's stem. As it waters, the sunflower gently bends its golden head toward the robot, like a grateful bow; the robot looks up in delight. Moss, tiny terracotta pots, fluffy clouds below the island, warm golden rim lighting, tactile clay and brushed-metal textures, shallow depth of field. Medium-wide composition keeps the entire robot, watering stream, and sunflower visible. Very slow gentle camera push-in. Sweet, magical, cinematic, coherent proportions and continuous action. No text, no captions, no cuts.
